system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## The "[STANDARD]" labels and Reviewer Efficiency Note

The Seller's cover note says that items marked [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have not relied on either statement.** Nothing in the record shows the Buyer agreed to these positions, and the labels are the Seller's own. Every item below has been reviewed on its merits.

The deal team should confirm with Wattlebridge's negotiators that no limitation or disclosure terms were conceded. The next mark-up should say expressly that the labels and the "accepted framework" statement are not agreed.

The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. It is now 5 November 2026, so every item needs a brought-down update before signing.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller position:** Cap of 20% of the price (AUD 4.8m) on general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 30–50% for general warranties, or 20% with W&I cover on top. Fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud must sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 35%, with an express carve-out of all non-general categories. **Reason:** 20% is within market only if the cap is truly confined to general warranties, which the Seller's drafting does not do (see SPA-N-014).

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller position:** De minimis of AUD 25k. Basket of AUD 250k, operating as a deductible (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of about AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated. Basket of about AUD 120–150k (0.5–0.6%) on a **tipping** basis, so recovery runs from the first dollar. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the AUD 25k de minimis only if series and related claims aggregate. Reject the deductible and move to a tipping basket of AUD 150k. **Reason:** A AUD 250k deductible stacked on a high de minimis takes out a large share of realistic warranty loss for a business of this size.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller position:** 18 months for general claims, plus a sweeping clause that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general claims, covering at least two audit cycles. Tax should run 5–7 years, or the amended assessment period plus 6 months. Title and capacity should run 7 years or the statutory limitation period. The sweeping clause should be deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the sweeping clause. **Reason:** The sweeping clause silently imposes 18 months on tax, title and the indemnities.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of 100% of price (AUD 24m) and a 7-year or statutory period. No de minimis, basket or disclosure against these warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. **Reason:** Title is the core of what Wattlebridge is buying, and capping recovery on it at AUD 4.8m is off-market.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out of fraud, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or agents from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on the carve-out; this is non-negotiable. **Reason:** Without it the Seller can argue that even fraudulent misstatement is capped and time-barred. Also note that Australian Consumer Law s 18 claims can be affected by non-reliance drafting.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, meeting a "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope" standard. Data room disclosure, if conceded at all, should be limited to an agreed, indexed, USB-archived set. There should be no deemed disclosure of public records beyond named ASIC, PPSR and court searches on stated dates. Disclosure must never qualify fundamental warranties, tax, or the specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Also delete DL 1.4, the "no admission of materiality/required" wording, so far as it would undercut indemnities. **Reason:** General disclosure combined with the knowledge qualifier in SPA-N-007 would neutralise most of the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was *discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-sandbagging clause, so that Buyer knowledge does not bar a claim. Failing that, the bar should apply only to *actual* knowledge of named Buyer deal leads, excluding advisers and constructive or discoverable knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete the clause, with actual knowledge of named individuals as the fallback. **Reason:** As drafted it bars claims on every issue the Buyer's own diligence flagged, including items 8–13 below.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent exists and that the clause 11.3 conditions are unverified.
- **Buyer should want:** A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer. The obligation should be all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, and Bluefen's ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%) justifies a long-stop right to terminate or reprice.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as a hard CP, with no deemed satisfaction. **Reason:** Bluefen accounts for 30% of revenue, and a consent that carries unmet conditions can still trigger termination after Completion.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller position:** A release "to be provided following Completion." The facility of ~AUD 3.2m is unpaid and the security is undischarged.
- **Buyer should want:** A payout letter and a deed of release delivered **at** Completion. The amount should be repaid from the price as Debt, as the deal is debt-free. PPSR and other security discharges should be lodged or delivered in escrow, and ASIC charge records updated. The Buyer should also confirm that Riverlark holds no security over the Sale Shares themselves.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release and make payout and release a Completion deliverable. **Reason:** Under the change-control clause (cl 8.1) Completion could itself trigger default, and the Buyer would own a company with live security over its assets.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420k in Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and does not appear in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** All bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding and other on-costs, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from the price, or paid by the Company and funded from Seller proceeds at Completion. This should be backed by a specific indemnity outside the cap and threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Add the bonuses to the funds flow as a deduction and grant an indemnity for any residual or deferred amounts. **Reason:** The employer is the Company, so unless the bonuses are itemised they become a roughly AUD 450k+ liability inherited by the Buyer.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A CP or Completion deliverable consisting of evidence that every SOW3 fee has cleared and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of the SOW3 Project Materials.
  - An indemnity covering *all* loss arising from any failure of title to, or claim over, the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, re-development cost and lost revenue, outside the cap and time limits.
  - Any unpaid amount (AUD 180k is recorded as open) treated as Debt.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity and make the confirmatory assignment a condition. **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 title does not pass until payment clears, so the exposure is to the IP itself, not only the AUD 180k fee.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." It is uncharacterised and no loss is stated.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Before Completion, a completed assessment under Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC (Notifiable Data Breaches). That 30-day assessment window from 22 September has likely passed, so the Buyer should confirm whether the OAIC and affected individuals have been notified.
  - Forensic confirmation of whether the file was accessed, and the recipient's deletion confirmation.
  - A specific indemnity, not qualified by disclosure or knowledge, for regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. It should have a separate cap, with a minimum survival of 3 years.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require a specific indemnity plus pre-Completion evidence. **Reason:** The exposure involves ~1,240 personal-information records with unknown access, so materiality cannot yet be assessed.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure of whether each renewal is terminable, the term, the commitment, and the business rationale. The Buyer should consider whether the split into three equal renewals avoided a board or approval threshold or ordinary-course covenants. A warranty that the renewals were within authority and on arm's-length terms is needed, and any prepaid or committed amounts not delivered should be captured in the completion accounts or locked-box leakage.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept them as ordinary course without evidence, and add a specific warranty and the Buyer's right to require termination where possible. **Reason:** Three related identical renewals suggest contract-splitting, and the Seller itself says they should be "read together."

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single regime, under which "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" and the limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** Separate, express regimes for each category:

| Category | Cap | Thresholds | Time limit | Disclosure applies? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 35% | De minimis / tipping basket | 24 months | Specific disclosure only |
| Fundamental (title, capacity) | 100% | None | 7 years | No |
| Tax warranties/indemnity | 100% | None | 5–7 years | No |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark) | 100% or bespoke | None | Bespoke | No |
| Fraud | Unlimited | None | None | No |

- **Recommendation:** Restructure clauses 12–13 into these category-specific limitations. **Reason:** The blanket drafting is the mechanism that pulls title, tax and the indemnities under the AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month limit.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification through an ASIC company extract cross-checked against the register, the constitution, share certificates or the issue history, and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP grants or pre-emptive rights.
  - An unqualified, uncapped title warranty that the shares are free of Encumbrances.
  - Completion deliverables: signed share transfers, original certificates, and releases of any security over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. Complete the searches and keep the title warranty fully unqualified. **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure (DL 10) concedes the Buyer has not verified title, and a self-maintained register is not proof.

## SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses and any Division 7A, GST or R&D exposures, with a 5–7 year limit, uncapped up to the price, and not subject to disclosure or thresholds.
  - Full IP warranties covering ownership, contractor and employee assignments (Ironquay and others) and open-source compliance, with a 3–4 year limit and a cap above the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as **open**, not settled. **Reason:** No agreed position on them appears in the record, and the "general regime" would cap and time-bar them at levels unsuitable for an analytics business whose value lies in its IP and data.

---

### Other points to note
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller's readings, that a notification is not a consent and an assignment restriction is not a change-of-control trigger, appear plausible. Counsel should confirm them against the full clauses, and the lease notification should be made a Completion deliverable.
- **Bring-down:** The Disclosure Letter needs updating from 22 September 2026, and the Buyer should require a Completion-date bring-down of the warranties, with no updated disclosure that cures breaches without a Buyer remedy.
=== END ADVICE ===
